name: North Fork Flathead
gaugeName: N F Flathead nr Columbia Falls
blurb: Wild & Scenic water along the Glacier boundary. Logjams, gravel bars, and Polebridge pie.

sections.notes: Launch at the downstream Polebridge access. Coal Creek is a side-channel landing; low water and wood may complicate the take-out. Scout before committing to the channel.

distanceEvidence.sourceName: Flathead Rivers Alliance / DREAM river access surveys (April 2026)
distanceEvidence.note: Approximate distance between the published access-survey river mile markers. Braids, water level and the landing used can change the paddled distance. Individual access surveys with coordinates and photographs are linked from the map markers.

sections.notes: Coal Creek launches from a side channel; wood and low water can require lining or dragging boats. Big Creek is a developed access with a day-use fee.

sections.notes: Includes the lower canyon rapids and the Shelf/Ledge above Glacier Rim. Scout and use whitewater skills; this is not a casual tube float. Great Northern Flats is an earlier exit before the lower rapids; confirm its access separately.

notices.title: Lower canyon whitewater
notices.text: Published paddler accounts describe Class III rapids between roughly river miles 9 and 4, within this section. Difficulty and the Shelf/Ledge hazard vary with flow; an access map does not identify a safe channel.
notices.sourceName: Rocky Mountain Canoe Club, July 2024 firsthand North Fork trip report, pp. 4–6
